sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The original records "Not known"; the alate of this species has not been described.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dark reddish wood-brown, the pronotum and antennae slightly paler; legs and abdominal tergites paler than the pronotum. Colour and general appearance very similar to H. rubriceps var. opacus, but easily distinguished by the sharp mandibular teeth, which are barb-like. Head (Fig. 281) more or less square, narrowing anteriorly. Labrum relatively small, rather pointed. Antennae 17-segmented; segments 3 and 4 shortest, or segment 4 shorter than segment 3; the remaining segments long and slender. Measurements (mm): body length 6.00; head length including mandibles (mandibles crossed at the tooth) 2.77; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.50; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.96; head width 1.55—1.61; pronotum length 0.44—0.47; pronotum width 0.92—0.96.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the original combination is Hamitermes clarki Hill, 1935 (the OCR mostly reads darki/elarki), the heading reads Hamitermes (Drepanotermes) darki Hill, and the species is now placed in Drepanotermes. Measurements in mm. Distribution: Eradu, Western Australia. The original records that the species is known only from the type series—3 soldiers, collected together with a colony of E. rubriceps var. opacus; type specimen: soldier holotype in C.S.I.R. The measurements are based on only 3 type specimens, hence mostly single values.
